acceptance_criteria: AC1: New module `src/commit_investigator/localization/blame_localizer.py` with function `localize_via_fix_diff(repo_path, fix_hash, file_extensions) -> list[StrategyHit]` that: (a) runs git diff-tree to find files changed by fix commit, (b) filters to source file extensions, (c) parses unified diff hunks for old-side line ranges, (d) runs git blame at fix_hash~1 on those lines, (e) returns unique SHAs as StrategyHit objects with strategy='localization_blame'
AC2: `localization_blame` added to VALID_STRATEGIES in strategies.py
AC3: Integration in prepare.py: when fix_hash is provided (eval mode), call blame_localizer, merge results with retrieval hits via existing merge_hits()
AC4: RetrievalConfig gains optional `fix_hash: str | None = None` field for eval-mode localization
AC5: prepare_investigation() accepts optional fix_hash parameter and passes it through
AC6: Additive: if fix_hash is None or blame produces no hits, pipeline runs unchanged (zero regression risk)
AC7: File type filter includes .java, .groovy, .scala, .py, .sh and excludes CHANGES.txt, .md, .xml
AC8: All existing tests pass (python -m pytest --tb=short -q)
AC9: New unit tests for blame_localizer covering: (a) normal blame hit, (b) no source files in fix diff, (c) empty hunks, (d) SHA normalization
edge_cases: Fix commit only touches non-source files (e.g., SPARK-20123 .sh files) — should return empty hits, not error
Fix commit touches 50+ files (large refactor) — should still work within reasonable time
Blame returns boundary commits (^sha) — should be filtered out
Fix hash doesn't exist in repo — should handle gracefully
verification_method: pytest + n=20 eval (Hit@5 target 0.800, no regression on existing hits)
eval_result: Hit@5=0.650 (13/20), Recall@100=1.000 (20/20), MRR=0.389. Below 0.800 target but Recall@100 structurally fixed. 339/339 tests pass.
